links.outcome: Effect of cumulative selection criteria on ML metrics (AUC, calibration) and epidemiological associations
links.effect: Sample fell from n=17,705 to n=4,256 (24.0%); cancer-depression OR attenuated from 1.78 to 1.39 (lost significance); AUC rose with selection but not after multiple-comparison correction; calibration error increased for four of five models.

links.outcome: Selective prediction performance and abstention rate
links.effect: All five models: selective prediction at approximately 20% coverage; test AUC 0.90, 95% CI 0.85-0.95; abstained on approximately 80%.
links.quote: Model-embedded uncertainty succeeded only for XGBoost; with the decoupled XGBoost residual selector, all five models achieved selective prediction at approximately 20% coverage (test AUC 0.90, 95% CI 0.85-0.95), abstaining on approximately 80% of cases for individual safety.

screen.practice: selective prediction with abstention and routing to human evaluation
screen.reason: The study tests selective prediction (uncertainty-based gating where models abstain from uncertain predictions to route patients to human evaluation) as a safeguard to mitigate selection bias and unsafe predictions in primary-care depression screening.

primary.practice: selective prediction gating and triage routing based on uncertainty
